acceptance_criteria: Library size / total counts per sample reported and compared across the 6 B1(control) vs 6 B2(treated) samples
PCA or hierarchical clustering on normalized (e.g., log-CPM or vst) counts computed and PC1/PC2 coordinates reported per sample with condition/batch labels overlaid
Report explicitly states that condition and batch are perfectly confounded (same grouping variable) so any separation on PCA cannot be attributed to either factor alone
No batch-correction (ComBat, limma removeBatchEffect, SVA) is applied at this stage since it would be uninterpretable under complete confounding

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
caveats: Do not attempt ComBat, SVA, or a design with both batch and condition terms — with n=6/6 and perfect confounding these either fail to fit (rank-deficient) or silently absorb/remove the condition effect entirely
Any downstream consumer of this gene list must be told the confound cannot be resolved with this dataset; a follow-up experiment with condition and batch crossed would be needed to disambiguate
steps.question: Using DESeq2 on the raw integer counts (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 12 samples) with metadata.csv condition labels, which genes are differentially expressed between treated (batch B2) and control (batch B1)?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design ~ condition on raw counts (batch cannot be added as a covariate: batch is collinear with condition, model matrix would not be full rank, so a batch term is explicitly omitted with the reason stated)
Full results table (log2FoldChange, p-value, padj, baseMean) exported for all ~12000 genes
Number of genes at padj < 0.05 reported, along with top up/down genes by log2FoldChange

Output/report explicitly states, next to the DE results, that condition and batch B1/B2 are perfectly confounded, so every differential gene found is equally explainable by a batch/technical/processing effect as by the treatment itself — the design cannot separate the two explanations statistically
No claim of a deconfounded or batch-corrected treatment effect is made anywhere in this step's output

plan.title: DE analysis of confounded batch/condition lung RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The design has 6 treated vs 6 control samples where batch (B1=all controls, B2=all treated) is completely confounded with condition. This is a hard structural limitation: no statistical method — including DESeq2 with a batch term, ComBat, or SVA-derived surrogate variables — can distinguish a true treatment effect from a batch/technical effect when every treated sample sits in one batch and every control in the other. Any 'batch correction' applied here would either do nothing (batch and condition are the same column, so a model matrix including both is not full rank) or would remove the condition effect itself. The correct, honest response is: (1) run standard DESeq2 differential expression treated vs control on the raw counts, since that is the only fittable model, (2) explicitly flag every result as an unresolvable condition/batch confound rather than attempting a fix that would either fail numerically or launder the confound into an invisible false signal, (3) perform QC/exploratory diagnostics (library size, PCA) to characterize how much of the separation looks batch-associated vs biologically plausible, and (4) run pathway enrichment on the DE result for hypothesis generation only, with the caveat carried through. No step claims to deconfound what is structurally unresolvable.
